text:
Marathon Petroleum moved up just 0.24% today, but the real story is the 13.2% gain over two weeks riding a sharp spike in crude oil prices. US crude jumped to $101.91 per barrel—up from around $98 just yesterday—as Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint that carries roughly a third of global seaborne oil. Refiners like Marathon profit when crude prices rise, especially with the company running at high utilization (93.5% of US refinery capacity online) and able to turn that pricier oil into fuel faster than competitors.

The broader tailwind here is a tightening global energy market: Brent crude hit $110, tanker costs have surged (adding $38 per barrel to the real cost of moving oil), and diesel storage has tightened to 102.6 million barrels. These dynamics are pushing refining margins higher, even though the stock pulled back slightly on October 15th before recovering this week—suggesting traders are weighing upside profit potential against geopolitical uncertainty.
